entities.summary:
Bāyazīd Basṭāmī, commonly known as the Sultān-ul-Ārifīn, was a Persian Sufi who became famous for his bold articulation of fanāʾ–the Sufi notion of self-annihilation. Born in the late 8th century CE in the city of Basra, Iraq, Bāyazīd Basṭāmī was a key figure in the development of Sufi thought and practice. He was known for his charismatic leadership and his ability to inspire devotion in his followers. Bāyazīd Basṭāmī's teachings emphasized the importance of love, compassion, and self-surrender, and he attracted a large following of adherents who sought to live out his principles in their daily lives. Through his writings and teachings, Bāyazīd Basṭāmī helped to shape the spiritual landscape of the Islamic world during the medieval period.

Bāyazīd Basṭāmī's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime and continues to influence Sufi thought and practice to this day. His ideas about fanāʾ and the importance of self-surrender have been studied and debated by scholars and theologians for centuries. In addition, Bāyazīd Basṭāmī's writings have been translated into many languages and have helped to spread Sufi ideas across the world.

Despite his significant impact on Sufi thought and practice, Bāyazīd Basṭāmī's life and teachings remain somewhat mysterious. There is little concrete information about his early life or his relationships with other prominent figures of the time. However, his writings and teachings continue to inspire and guide millions of people around the world.

Bāyazīd Basṭāmī's teachings on fanāʾ have been influential in shaping Islamic mysticism and spirituality. His ideas about the importance of self-surrender and the need to transcend the ego have resonated with many people across cultures and traditions. In addition, Bāyazīd Basṭāmī's emphasis on the importance of love and compassion has helped to promote a more inclusive and compassionate form of spirituality.
